newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar issues decree allowing offshore banking.
newsitem.headline: Qatar issues decree allowing offshore banking.

text.p: Qatar's crown prince has issued a decree amending bank laws to allow the Central Bank to licence offshore banking units, the Bank's governor said on Wednesday.
"It is intended to upgrade the banking system and diversify the market to open more avenues of profit-making for banks," Abdullah bin Khaled al-Attiyah told Reuters.
The decree, issued by Crown Prince Sheikh Jassim bin Hamad al-Thani on Monday, takes effect on October 4.
"The facility will be initially offered to Qatari local banks and investment firms to enable them to open offshore operations," Attiyah said.
He said offshore units will not be allowed to accept deposits from Qatari nationals or expatriate residents except in special circumstances and after Central Bank authorisation.
"The offshore banking units will be exempt from taxes," Attiyah said.
In Qatar, foreign banks are required to pay tax on a sliding scale from 10 percent up if their annual profit exceeds 500,000 riyals ($137,362). Local banks are tax exempt.

"The move to allow offshore banking is part of an overall strategy to reform the financial market and expand investment banking in the state," said Central Bank Deputy Governor Sheikh Abdullah bin Saud al-Thani.
Qatar has a small financial market with commercial bank deposits totalling some 22.1 billion riyals in March.
But its huge gas reserves -- the third largest in the world, after Russia and Iran -- have lured foreign banks to do business in its burgeoning gas industry.
Local bankers said the opening of offshore banks would help attract more overseas funds.
The Gulf's main financial centre is in nearby Bahrain.
